name: Computer Science
description: The Computer Science pathway teaches programming, cybersecurity, and networking. Students start with AP Computer Science Principles, then branch into AP Computer Science A and/or AP Cybersecurity before converging on AP Networking.

courses.title: AP Computer Science Principles
courses.desc: AP Computer Science Principles is an introductory college-level computing course that introduces students to the breadth of the field of computer science. Students learn to design and evaluate solutions and to apply computer science to solve problems through the development of algorithms and programs. They incorporate abstraction into programs and use data to discover new knowledge. Students also explain how computing innovations and computing systems—including the internet—work, explore their potential impacts, and contribute to a computing culture that is collaborative and ethical. At Walton, students write their programs in Java, building a foundation for AP Computer Science A.

courses.title: AP Computer Science A
courses.desc: Java-based programming, data structures, and object-oriented design.

courses.title: AP Cybersecurity
courses.desc: AP Cybersecurity trains students in the field and aligns closely with standard first-year collegiate cybersecurity courses.

courses.title: AP Networking
courses.desc: Network design, protocols, and infrastructure, AP-level.
